title: Congregational Care
definition: Congregational Care is the shared ministry of watching over, comforting, encouraging, correcting, and helping one another in the body of Christ.
summary: The whole Church participates in caring for Christ's people.
christFocus: Jesus Christ cares for His sheep and teaches His people to love one another as He has loved them.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Congregational Care teaches that Christ does not redeem people into isolation but into a gathered, accountable, worshiping, serving, and mission-shaped people. The Church belongs to Jesus, is formed by the Gospel, and is strengthened by the Word, prayer, ordinances, fellowship, and Spirit-empowered service.

This doctrine helps believers see the Church as more than a place to attend. It is the household of God, the body of Christ, and a visible witness to the grace, holiness, unity, and truth of the Lord.

The specific emphasis here is the whole church participates in caring for christ's people.. A healthy church life displays Christ's care for His people and His mission to the world.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because many people treat church as optional, consumer-driven, or disconnected from discipleship. Congregational Care calls believers back to Christ's design for His people, where worship, truth, love, accountability, service, and mission are held together.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Participate in church life with humility and faithfulness. Let congregational care move you to serve, forgive, gather, pray, give, submit to Scripture, care for others, and help the body of Christ grow in love and maturity.
